issues.description: Method addGuestStudents(int): the problem statement UML declares the method as returning void (problem_statement.md line 73), and the task text describes adding guest students (problem_statement.md lines 49-51). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 90) declares the method as public boolean addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and returns a boolean. The template only contains a TODO for adding the method (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 18) and instructs students to implement it "as specified in the task and the UML." This inconsistency between the UML/specification (void) and the solution (boolean) will confuse students about the expected signature and behavior and may cause mismatches with tests or example usages.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Two viable options:

Option A (preferable if boolean semantics are desired): Update the problem statement UML and the task description to declare addGuestStudents(int): boolean and document the semantics (e.g., return true on success, return false for invalid input). Update the template to include the method signature public boolean addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents); and update any tests/examples to expect a boolean.

Option B (if the specification must be preserved): Change the solution implementation to match the UML by making addGuestStudents(int) return void. Update the solution method body to perform the addition without returning a value and remove boolean returns. Also update the solution comments and any example usages accordingly.

After choosing one option, ensure the template, problem statement (UML and descriptive text), and solution are all updated to use the same signature and documented behavior so students have a single, unambiguous expectation.
